📡 Pezeshkian offers condolences over deadly bus crash, calls for probe

📌 Tehran, IRNA –President Masoud Pezeshkian has expressed condolences to the families of the victims of a bus crash in the western Iranian province of Ilam Province, that killed a dozen people and injured several more.

In a message addressed to the families of the victims and their colleagues on Sunday, Pezeshkian conveyed sympathy over the deadly accident involving Dehloran Petro-refinery employees.
​
He said that the relevant authorities had been tasked with taking immediate action to provide all necessary medical care for the injured, offering comfort to the bereaved families, and conducting a thorough and transparent investigation into the incident.
​
The tragic bus rollover involving the hardworking refinery employees, which resulted in the loss of life and injuries to several people, caused me deep sorrow and grief, Pezeshkian underscored.
​
The President emphasized that safeguarding the lives and well-being of the workforce is a serious responsibility that necessitates steps to identify and eliminate the underlying factors behind such incidents, thereby preventing any recurrence.
​
Twelve people were killed, and sixteen others were injured when the bus carrying oil company employees overturned on Saturday.

🔻 Russia says Western pressure on Iran undermines IAEA impartiality

📌 London, IRNA – Russia has criticized Western countries for exploiting the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) safeguards system to exert political pressure on Iran, warning that their actions are undermining the agency’s impartiality and escalating tensions over Tehran’s peaceful nuclear program.

Mikhail Ulyanov, Russia’s permanent representative to international organizations in Vienna, made the remarks in an interview with the Russian newspaper Kommersant published on Sunday, ahead of the IAEA Board of Governors’ quarterly meeting.
​
Ulyanov said Western countries were using the safeguards system as a political tool against countries they opposed, undermining its technical foundations and the principle of neutrality. He said Russia and like-minded countries were working to preserve the transparency and technical and legal credibility of safeguards procedures.
​
The Russian diplomat also criticized the Western-led approach at the IAEA Board of Governors and the UN Security Council, saying political maneuvering by Western majorities in both bodies had taken precedence over genuine efforts to resolve differences with Iran.
​
Addressing a September resolution by the IAEA Board of Governors demanding access for inspectors to all Iranian nuclear facilities, Ulyanov said the resolution came while Iran has been repeatedly under US and Israeli military threats. He warned that any attack on facilities hosting international inspectors could put their lives in direct danger.
​
He said the United States and the European troika of Britain, France and Germany had used their numerical advantage on the Board of Governors to seek referral of the resolution to the UN Security Council, a move he said would only heighten tensions without producing constructive results.
​
Ulyanov also rejected recent US allegations of secret Iranian nuclear activities at the so-called Pickaxe Mountain site, noting that the IAEA had never issued a report on the facility and, to Russia’s knowledge, had no information confirming nuclear activities there.
​
He said Washington had failed to provide credible evidence to support its allegations.
​
The IAEA Board of Governors is scheduled to begin its quarterly meeting in Vienna on November 18, with Iran among the key issues on its agenda.
​
Iran has consistently stressed the peaceful nature of its nuclear program and its commitment to obligations under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT).
​
Tehran has maintained that the resumption of normal safeguards cooperation requires an end to military threats and the establishment of necessary security conditions.

Weapons Seizure in Beirut’s Dahiyeh: A Significant Security Achievement or a False Impression of Progress in Disarming Hezbollah?

On November 13, the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) published photographs of weapons and ammunition seized during a raid on a warehouse in the al-Musharrafieh area of Beirut’s Dahiyeh. The LAF described the operation as a “high-quality security operation” and emphasized that a large quantity of weapons had been seized.

However, considering the quantity and characteristics of the weapons seized, it is difficult to regard this operation as a significant achievement. The weapons are of very limited quality, military value, and quantity. Even if the seized weapons do belong to Hezbollah (based on the circumstantial evidence of the warehouse’s location, north of Haret Hreik and east of Ghobeiry), their seizure has no meaningful operational impact on the organization’s military capabilities. The LAF did not attribute the seized weapons to Hezbollah, and the operation was presented as part of its efforts to combat arms trafficking.

As during the ceasefire period from November 2024 to February 2026, we continue to witness an enormous gap between the Lebanese Armed Forces’ public reports of weapons seizures and the reality on the ground. The false impression of progress persists.

The Lebanese Armed Forces are not systematically working to dismantle Hezbollah’s military power. Highly limited, isolated weapons seizures, even in the heart of the Dahiyeh (assuming the weapons do belong to Hezbollah), are no substitute for dismantling the organization’s weapons arsenal, military infrastructure, and military control.

This is even before addressing additional questions: Was the operation coordinated with Hezbollah? Are the seized weapons eventually returned to Hezbollah through a revolving-door mechanism?
